newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says aims to clarify policy pattern.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says aims to clarify policy pattern.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank (central bank) said on Thursday it was seeking to clarify a new pattern for its monetary policy and break the market's fortnightly focus on the bank's reverse repurchase tenders.
"We don't want to have a focus every Tuesday about what information will come out," bank governor Urban Backstrom told a news conference.
"It is not the pattern, but the incoming information that we should be looking at."

In recent months the Riksbank has cut its key interest rate, the repo rate, every other weeks, most recently by 10 basis points. So far it has cut the repo 22 times this year, from 8.91 percent at the start of the year.

But the bank departed from this pattern on Thursday, announcing a 25 basis point cut in the repo rate to 4.60 percent for next Tuesday's operation, a level it said would remain unchanged for the next three reverse repurchase operations.
Backstrom said the recent inflation levels had made the Riksbank more optimistic and the bank needed more time to analyse the new information.
